# Open Door Learning

> Jonathan Malkin, AI educator and builder in Austin, Texas. He works with owners and executives who are using AI and want to make it more useful in their business. He teaches them and their teams to solve real business problems with AI, and builds solutions when needed.

## About

Jonathan Malkin teaches hands-on AI workshops for owners, executives and their teams, working as Open Door Learning. Each person works on a real task from their own week, on their own laptop, with help beside them, and leaves with something that works: a working tool or workflow, a skill applied to their own work, or a clear decision about where to start. He spent more than twenty years in enterprise technology, including eight years at Automation Anywhere, before going independent in June 2025. He is based in Austin and teaches in person there. He also teaches online; online sessions are shaped for a call, so their format and content differ from the in-person workshops.

## Who it is for

- Owners and executives who have tried AI and want it to do real work in the business.
- Hosts: chambers, associations, peer groups, co-working communities and portfolios that gather owners and executives and want useful AI education for their members.
- Event organizers and podcast hosts looking for a practical speaker on AI in business.

## Workshops

Three kinds of room. Most sessions run ninety minutes; the technical one can run a half day. Details and a message form: https://builtwithjon.com/workshops/

Hands-on build workshops (laptops open, one real task each):
- Put Your Business Knowledge to Work: a shared reference the team and their AI can both use.
- Build One Useful AI Workflow: a repeatable method for one recurring task.
- Build Your Personal AI Assistant: an assistant set up for meeting preparation, next steps and a daily brief.
- Hand Off Your First Task to an AI Agent: one recurring task running under the participant’s own approval rules, and a short list of what an agent may and may not do.

Leadership sessions (no laptops; decisions written down):
- See Where AI Could Help Your Business: a short list of places to start, drawn from the participant's own week.
- Set Your Team’s AI Direction: a one-page AI direction for the team: the rules, three first projects with owners, and what to check in ninety days.

For IT and technical teams:
- Give Your AI Agents a Map: a folder structure and instruction files an agent can find its way around, running with two tools on the team's own files.
